title: Taxpayer Notification and Privacy Act

claims.claim: Under current law the IRS must notify the taxpayer in advance before seeking third-party information
claims.sourceSpan: before contact is made with such other persons
claims.note: Structural inference: bill amends the existing 7602(c) third-party-contact notice paragraph (redesignates its subparagraphs), which presupposes an existing advance-notice regime.

claims.claim: Current law does not require the IRS to identify the specific information it is seeking
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons
claims.note: The bill adds the specificity duty, implying current law lacks it.

claims.claim: the third party is described as “like your employer or bank”
claims.sourceSpan: information sought to be obtained from such other persons
claims.note: Employer/bank examples are not in the bill text (source says only “such other persons” / “a person other than the taxpayer”); illustrative gloss drawn from the CR floor quote, not the bill.

claims.claim: This bill requires the IRS to identify each specific item of information it intends to collect from the third party
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: and give the taxpayer at least 45 days to provide it themselves
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 45 days

claims.claim: this applies whenever the IRS has not already asked the taxpayer for it and the taxpayer could reasonably provide it
claims.sourceSpan: has not been previously requested from the taxpayer and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer

claims.claim: Exception one: the rule does not cover tax collection proceedings
claims.sourceSpan: such information is sought with respect to the collection of a tax liability
claims.note: Source says “collection of a tax liability”; “proceedings” is an added gloss but the collection carve-out is present.

claims.claim: Exception two: the Secretary can waive it when third-party contact is deemed necessary
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary determines that such information is necessary notwithstanding whether the taxpayer could independently provide such information
claims.note: Source frames necessity of the information; summary says contact necessary - minor object shift, same effect. Scope here is limited to the specificity rule, which is correct.

claims.claim: Requires the IRS to tell taxpayers exactly what information it plans to collect from third parties
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.claim: give them 45 days to provide it first
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 45 days
claims.note: Brief states “45 days” flatly; source is a floor (“not less than 45 days”) - minor loss of the floor qualifier.

claims.claim: Specific Notice Required
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.sourceSpan: has not been previously requested from the taxpayer and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer

claims.claim: Taxpayers get at least 45 days to respond - more if they request it with reasonable cause
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 45 days (or more, if the taxpayer requests additional time and shows reasonable cause)

claims.claim: Exceptions
claims.sourceSpan: shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer

claims.sourceSpan: such information is sought with respect to the collection of a tax liability
claims.note: Correctly limits the waiver to the SPECIFICITY requirement (unlike the Section 2 detail and underreported, which wrongly extend it to the 45-day period). “proceedings” is a minor gloss.

claims.claim: Names the Act the “Taxpayer Notification and Privacy Act”
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the Taxpayer Notification and Privacy Act

claims.claim: Amends Section 7602(c)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to require the IRS to identify each specific item of information sought from a third party
claims.sourceSpan: Paragraph (1) of section 7602(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended

claims.claim: when that information has not been previously requested from the taxpayer and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer
claims.sourceSpan: has not been previously requested from the taxpayer and could reasonably be provided by the taxpayer

claims.claim: The advance notice must provide a period of not less than 45 days (or more on reasonable cause) to respond, including by providing the information themselves, before the IRS contacts the third party
claims.sourceSpan: a period of not less than 45 days (or more, if the taxpayer requests additional time and shows reasonable cause) to respond, including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B), before contact is made with such other persons

claims.claim: The exception in Section 7602(c)(3)(B) provides that the specificity requirement does not apply in the stated cases
claims.sourceSpan: shall not apply to information sought from a person other than the taxpayer

claims.claim: ...and that the WAITING PERIOD requirement (the 45-day notice) also does not apply under the exception
claims.sourceSpan: so much of subparagraph (C) of paragraph (1) as relates to such subparagraph (B)
claims.note: MATERIAL. The exception waives only subparagraph (B) (specificity) plus “so much of subparagraph (C) ... as relates to such subparagraph (B)” - i.e. the “including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B)” clause. The general “reasonable opportunity and a period of not less than 45 days ... to respond ... before contact is made” in (C) is NOT waived by this exception. Analysis overstates waiver scope.

claims.claim: ...if the information is sought for collection of a tax liability
claims.sourceSpan: such information is sought with respect to the collection of a tax liability

claims.claim: ...or if the Secretary determines the third-party information is necessary regardless of whether the taxpayer could provide it
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary determines that such information is necessary notwithstanding whether the taxpayer could independently provide such information

claims.claim: Effective date: 12 months after enactment
claims.sourceSpan: 12 months after the date of the enactment of this Act

claims.claim: The bill’s specificity requirement does not apply whenever the Secretary determines the third-party information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary determines that such information is necessary notwithstanding whether the taxpayer could independently provide such information

claims.claim: The bill’s 45-day notice requirement does not apply whenever the Secretary determines the third-party information is necessary
claims.sourceSpan: so much of subparagraph (C) of paragraph (1) as relates to such subparagraph (B)
claims.note: MATERIAL. The (c)(3)(B)(ii) necessity trigger waives only subparagraph (B) plus the (B)-related portion of (C); it does NOT waive the 45-day response period. Separately, (C) can be set aside via its own lead-in “except as otherwise provided by the Secretary,” which carries NO necessity condition - so the 45-day waiver is neither in this exception nor conditioned on necessity.

claims.claim: ...without any standard for what constitutes necessity or any procedural check on that determination
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary determines that such information is necessary notwithstanding whether the taxpayer could independently provide such information
claims.note: Accurate observation of absence - source states no standard or review.

claims.claim: The bill is framed as expanding taxpayer notification rights
claims.sourceSpan: provide for specific taxpayer notice when information is sought from third parties

claims.claim: The necessity exception allows the IRS to bypass both the itemized notice and the 45-day waiting period entirely based on the Secretary’s own judgment
claims.sourceSpan: so much of subparagraph (C) of paragraph (1) as relates to such subparagraph (B)
claims.note: MATERIAL. The necessity exception does not bypass the 45-day waiting period “entirely” - only subparagraph (B) and the (B)-related portion of (C) are waived. “entirely” compounds the overstatement.

claims.claim: ...with no defined standard, independent review, or notification to the taxpayer that the exception has been invoked
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary determines that such information is necessary notwithstanding whether the taxpayer could independently provide such information

claims.claim: Bill gives 45 days to respond but does not specify whether the IRS is barred from contacting the third party if the taxpayer provides the information within the window
claims.sourceSpan: to respond, including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B), before contact is made with such other persons
claims.note: Accurate: source sets a timing floor before contact, not a bar on contact upon early provision.

claims.claim: Bill does not address the taxpayer’s right to receive notice that the Secretary has invoked the necessity exception
claims.sourceSpan: the Secretary determines that such information is necessary notwithstanding whether the taxpayer could independently provide such information

claims.claim: Adds Section 7602(c)(1)(B): requirement for IRS to identify each specific item of information sought from a third party when not previously requested from the taxpayer
claims.sourceSpan: identifies each specific item of information intended to be sought from such persons

claims.sourceSpan: for himself and Mr. Panetta

claims.claim: Analysis omits subparagraph (C)’s opening qualifier “except as otherwise provided by the Secretary,” a broad, unconditioned Secretary override of the reasonable-opportunity / 45-day response requirement
claims.sourceSpan: except as otherwise provided by the Secretary
claims.note: MATERIAL. The Section 2 detail quotes (C) but drops this lead-in, and the underreported thesis on Secretary discretion misses that (C) itself lets the Secretary set aside the 45-day/opportunity requirement with NO necessity finding - arguably a broader escape hatch than the (c)(3)(B) exception the analysis highlights.

notes: Source file data/bill-text/119-HR-6495.txt is the INTRODUCED (IH, 2025-12-05) version; the analysis body faithfully tracks that text. However versions[] show the bill PASSED the House as ENGROSSED (2026-04-27) and the cache versionChanges asserts the engrossed text materially differs (specificity narrowed to info “related to determining tax liability”; two-prong exception collapsed to a single Secretary-necessity prong; the “including by providing the information described in subparagraph (B)” clause and the standalone “collection of a tax liability” exception removed). Those engrossed-version claims CANNOT be verified against the provided source (Introduced only) and were not judged here; the passed text should be re-fetched and re-audited. Core material finding: the (c)(3)(B) exception waives only subparagraph (B) plus “so much of subparagraph (C) ... as relates to such subparagraph (B),” not the whole 45-day waiting period - repeated in the Section 2 detail and twice in underreported. featured_quotes (Steube CR floor quote) not judged: no Congressional Record source provided; cannot verify against bill text.
